questions.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y={4}^{x-5}+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- First, we plot the graph of $y={4}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/04dbe1b44e4fe148d225f1d4f61f104d34892d2e0328c3c59c6f9afd27d0dfbb.png)

- To plot $y={4}^{x-5},$ we shift the graph of $y={4}^{x}$ horizontally by $5$ units to the right. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(5,1),$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/850e48a9d19ff643277b356140f18f264f5a729191eb2812f1aa472d131c0df1.png)

- To plot $y={4}^{x-5}+1,$ we shift the graph of $y={4}^{x-5}$ vertically by $1$ unit up. The point $(5,1)$ moves to $(5,2)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/a38af6a1d1dabc4727d08ec452ad5c9efe631b4ba08b68291318672bb34a990b.png)
